executive_summary: EUR/USD trades at 1.16258 (payload close, 2026-09-03), up 0.62% over one month, 0.81% over three and 0.45% over six, but down 2.03% over twelve, and sits at the 43rd percentile of its 52-week closing range of 1.13586–1.19773. The dominant bilateral narrative is not divergence but a race between two hiking central banks, and the entire tactical edge lies in the fact that only one of the two hikes is still available to be priced: the 10 September ECB decision is discounted at roughly 97% while the 16 September FOMC sits at 57–66% in futures against a June dot median that implies the move outright. That asymmetry is what carries the settled tactical verdict — Bearish, conviction 3, net score −0.2158 — and it is corroborated by a 25-delta risk reversal that is bid for euro downside at every tenor (−0.377 at 38.6 days) and by same-direction speculative positioning: net short euro at −36,352 contracts and net long dollar at +18,682. The strategic verdict is Neutral, conviction 2, net score +0.0192, because a policy differential whose direction of travel narrows from −137.5bp toward −87.5bp on the Fed's own 2027 dot, plus a materially worse US fiscal trajectory, is almost exactly offset by a European winter energy bill against 62.99% storage and an unhedged year-end dollar funding turn. The bilateral facts that do not appear in either standalone dossier are these: the euro area runs its single largest goods surplus with the United States at $193.3bn, yet the pair has no offsetting terms-of-trade leg on energy, because the importer is the base currency and the exporter is the quote currency. The honest caveat is that the pair's own chart disagrees with the tactical call — spot is above a rising 50-day and 100-day, has made higher lows since the 24 June low of 1.13239 and higher highs into 21 August, and September is historically one of the pair's stronger months with September historically the second-strongest month for EUR/USD performance — so the tactical short is a fade of price momentum, not a ride on it, and should be sized and stopped accordingly. We publish the settled direction as issued and flag the tension rather than resolving it in either direction.

market_context.valuation_assessment: There is no published PPP series for this pair in either dossier, so pair-level valuation is expressed as a real-effective relative and labelled as a proxy rather than a fair value. On BIS real effective exchange rates for June 2026 the euro stood at 102.69 against the dollar at 107.84, making the euro roughly 4.8% cheaper than the dollar in real effective terms and implying a REER-relative reference of about 1.2171 against a spot of 1.16258 — approximately 5.1% of undervaluation on that proxy. Both legs' dossiers agree on the direction and disagree on its usefulness: the euro's real effective rate has drifted 1.20 points lower over a year and sits mid-distribution, while the dollar's has moved only 0.21 points and is the fourth-richest reading in the G10+SGD set, so the dollar has been parked at an expensive real level for a year without correcting. The practical reading is that valuation is a permission slip for the strategic Neutral rather than an argument against the tactical short: a real-effective gap that has not closed in twelve months generates no timing signal over two to four weeks, and a closing percentile of 43 says the market has priced neither leg's structural story into the cross rate. What is priced at 1.16258 is a −137.5bp policy differential and nothing else — no discount for a European winter energy squeeze, no premium for a US primary income balance that has just flipped to deficit, and no premium for the reserve-share arithmetic on either side.

market_context.recent_regime: The regime is a low-volatility range in which the pair is being driven by the American leg rather than the European one. Both central banks turned hawkish in parallel rather than in opposition, so the differential has been static at −137.5bp while both curves repriced higher, and the pair's August range of roughly 1.1503 to 1.1711 was resolved almost entirely by Jackson Hole on 28 August. Underneath, the risk backdrop is the goldilocks configuration in which this pair historically rises — VIX at 14.43–14.51, investment-grade spreads at 79bp, high yield at 260–263bp, record European equities and a broad trade-weighted dollar down 1.69% on the month against a G10-only basket down 0.37% — yet the pair has advanced only 0.62% in that time, which says the rate differential is doing more work than the risk regime. The dominant near-term narrative is not about the euro at all: it is whether the Fed hikes on 16 September, and the market's own instruments are split, with futures at 57–66% and prediction markets at 48–55%.

bilateral_carry_analysis.carry_assessment: The bilateral policy differential is −137.5bp: the ECB deposit rate is 2.25% and the fed funds midpoint 3.625%, both as of 2026-09-01 in the gated store. A long EUR/USD position therefore pays away 137.5bp a year and a short earns it. At a spot of 1.16258 that is approximately 160 pips a year, 13 pips a month and 39 pips a quarter, against an ATR(14) of 46 pips — so carry consumes roughly 28% of one average day's range every month, material for a quarter and corrosive for a year. The carry-to-vol ratio is −0.238, computed as −1.375% annualised carry divided by the gated 3-month ATM implied volatility of 5.777% (measured at 94.7 days rather than 90, because CME lists quarterly). The sign is the noteworthy part: unusually for this pair, the carry sign and the settled tactical direction agree, which means spot is a defensible vehicle for the tactical short rather than options being the only sensible expression. The breakeven move is symmetric and small: spot must rise 13 pips a month for a long to break even on carry, or fall 13 pips a month for a short to break even against a flat spot. The forward curve charges essentially the same hurdle. The gated futures roll premium is 139.1bp annualised, observed 2026-08-31 over a 13.6-to-48.6-day window, which sits within two basis points of the 137.5bp policy differential — so by covered interest parity the cross-currency basis contributes only a couple of basis points, and that is independently corroborated by the CME three-month EUR/USD basis index at −0.81bp on 28 August against −40 to −80bp in historically stressed periods. The carry regime is working and there is no funding stress to disrupt it: realised volatility at 4.66%, credit at post-crisis tights, and a basis at zero is the exact environment in which carry accrues rather than being erased by gap moves. The regime risk is not that carry stops paying but that a single 2% gap on 10 or 16 September erases more than a year of it — 137.5bp is 160 pips, and a 2% move is 233 pips.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: The bilateral policy differential is -137.5bp: the ECB deposit rate is 2.25% and the fed funds midpoint 3.625%, both as of 2026-09-01 in the gated store. This is not a divergence trade, it is a race between two hiking central banks, and over the tactical window what matters is not who hikes but whose hike is already discounted. The ECB leg is effectively fully priced: OIS puts a 25bp move to 2.50% at the 10 September Governing Council, which carries a full projection round, at roughly 97%. The Fed leg is not: futures price the 16 September FOMC, which carries a Summary of Economic Projections, at roughly 57-66% for a move to 3.75-4.00%, and prediction markets carry it materially lower at 48-55%. That leaves essentially no surprise capacity on the European side of the pair and roughly 35-43 points of two-way capacity on the American side. The direction of that capacity is not symmetric either: the June SEP median of 3.80% for end-2026 implies the hike outright, so the Committee's own projection sits above the curve rather than below it, and the 2-year Treasury at 4.34% is 71.5bp above the funds midpoint, a front end that cannot be reconciled with a hold-then-cut path. Transmission is mechanical. If both banks deliver, the differential is unchanged at -137.5bp and the pair loses the one rate catalyst that was arguably euro-supportive; if the ECB delivers and the Fed holds, the differential narrows to -112.5bp and the pair rises. The expected-value skew sits with the dollar because the unpriced leg is the American one and the dots point one way. Carry reinforces it: long EUR/USD pays away 137.5bp a year, a carry-to-3m-implied-vol ratio of -0.238 against the gated 5.777% surface.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over one to six months the level argument gives way to the rate-of-change argument, and the rate of change is the one unambiguously euro-favourable leg in the strategic table. The ECB path runs 2.25% now, 2.50% at the 10 September projections round, and a further 25bp to 2.75% apparently discounted by early 2027 - fifty basis points of improvement from an institution that has already delivered once. The Fed path, on the Committee's own arithmetic, runs 3.625% now, a median of 3.80% for end-2026, and 3.60% for 2027: one more hike and then a cut. If both paths deliver as priced the differential narrows from -137.5bp toward -112.5bp by the 9 December FOMC and toward -87.5bp on the Fed's own 2027 dot, which is a mechanically higher EUR/USD. The dated decisions that would do it are the 9 December FOMC with its SEP and the 17 December ECB projection round, and any strategic policy thesis for this pair has to be judged against those two dates because nothing else in the window can move the differential. What caps confidence at 50 is that both terminals face downward revision risk from opposite directions and neither is a free option. The ECB's own negotiated wage tracker printed 2.1% for Q2 2026 against 3.2% in 2025 and its June projections have headline HICP back at 2.0% in 2028, which makes a 2.75% terminal demanding; equally, US core PCE has been stuck at 3.3% for three months, and a December SEP that removes the 2027 cut would convert a terminal Fed hike into a cycle and reverse the entire narrowing. So the direction of travel favours the pair, the magnitude is already in the strip, and the distribution around it is wide.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: This factor is a genuine standoff and the honest reading is that the two legs cancel. On growth the level differential favours the dollar and has not closed: US GDP 2.1% year on year against euro-area 1.0%, a 110bp gap, and an August composite PMI of 56.0 in the United States against 52.1 in the euro area. On inflation the level also favours the dollar in the sense that matters for a pair analysis, because higher inflation in a regime where both central banks are reacting to it means more tightening: US core PCE 3.3% and headline PCE 3.7% against euro-area HICPX at 2.5% and headline at 2.9% in July with a 3.3% August flash. On surprise direction, however, the euro area has the better run - German Ifo 88.8 against 87.2 expected, GfK -26.6 against -29.5, the Economic Sentiment Indicator 98.4 against 97.5, new orders at a 40-month high - while the United States has the worse labour print, with July payrolls at -23,000 against a +83,000 consensus and average hourly earnings at a five-year low of 3.2%. Asymmetric sensitivity runs one way: the 4 September payroll report and the 11 September CPI move this pair materially harder than any euro-area release, because they are what determines whether the 16 September FOMC can deliver. So the pair's data risk is concentrated on the quote leg and it is two-sided, with a soft payroll print being the single largest euro-positive datapoint available inside the tactical window and the strong US survey and price data being the offset. A factor whose level differential favours the dollar and whose surprise differential favours the euro, with the decisive prints still unpublished, is a Neutral rather than a directional input.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over one to six months the composition of each side's inflation matters more than its level, and both compositions are temporary in a way that roughly offsets. The euro area's overshoot is imported cost-push: energy contributed +0.94pp of the 2.9% July headline at +10.0% year on year, while food, alcohol and tobacco decelerated from 3.2% to 1.2% and negotiated wages printed 2.1% for Q2 2026 against 3.2% in 2025. Wages at that level cannot sustain services inflation at 3.3%, so the euro-area overshoot unwinds with the energy base effect. The United States' overshoot is substantially tariff-driven: the average statutory rate is 11.0% as at 24 August 2026, the highest since roughly the early 1940s, and the tell is that core PCE at 3.3% sits 80bp ABOVE core CPI at 2.5%, an inversion of the normal sign that points to pass-through concentrated in the goods and imputed components PCE weights most heavily. A tariff is a level shift, so it drops out of the year-on-year comparison too. Both disinflate; neither leg gains. On growth the trajectories converge modestly in the euro's favour - the euro area has a multi-year fiscal floor in the German programme, with a EUR500bn infrastructure fund and defence rising toward 3.5% of GDP by 2029, visible already in a manufacturing PMI of 54.1, while the United States is decelerating through the labour channel with participation at 61.4% and wage growth at a five-year low. But the euro-area recovery is narrow, with German services at 48.5 and the whole French composite at 48.8 in contraction, and US nominal momentum is real with GDPNow at 4.8% for Q3. Converging from a 110bp deficit is not the same as closing it, and Neutral is the correct output.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: EUR/USD is a low-beta risk pair by the framework's own classification, so the transmission here is not the carry-proxy channel that drives AUD/JPY but the dollar-smile channel: the dollar is the haven and the euro is the anti-dollar, so calm plus synchronised growth is where the pair rises and fear is where it falls. The current configuration is emphatically the former. The VIX closed at 14.43-14.51 in the last week of August, down from 20.66 a month earlier and having touched a 2026 low of 14.2; US investment-grade spreads are 79bp and high yield 260-263bp, the latter 21-27bp tighter on the month, both near post-crisis tights with no stress in any observable channel. European equities are leading rather than following, with the Euro Stoxx 50 at a record above 6,560 and the DAX above 26,450, which is a genuine portfolio-inflow channel for the base leg. Most directly, the broad dollar has been falling into all of this: the Federal Reserve's broad trade-weighted index fell 1.69-2.1% over the month while the DXY-weighted G10 basket fell only 0.37%, so the dollar has been losing ground and the euro is the largest single beneficiary of any dollar reallocation by construction, at 57.6% of the DXY. The offsets are real but do not reverse the sign over four weeks: gold rallying alongside a firm dollar suggests the standard inverse correlation is partially broken, and a VIX at 14.4 sitting on top of an active Gulf conflict is complacent rather than reassuring. Over two to four weeks the prevailing regime is the goldilocks zone in which this pair rises, and that is what the factor measures.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over one to six months this factor stops measuring the prevailing regime and starts measuring the distribution of regimes, and from a 2026-low VIX with credit at post-crisis tights that distribution is one-sided. The asymmetry is structural to the pair rather than a judgement about equities: the dollar is the risk-off beneficiary and the euro is explicitly not a haven, so every point of upward volatility surprise transmits as a lower EUR/USD, while the offsetting euro gains in a shock accrue against the commodity and high-carry bloc rather than against the dollar. There is essentially no room left for spreads to compress - 79bp investment grade and 260bp high yield are close to their floor - and the mean-reverting path from there widens them, which is dollar-positive. Three credible regime-shift candidates sit inside the window and two of them point the same way: a Middle East escalation that closes shipping is dollar-positive on both the haven and the energy-export channels; a long-end disorder episode from a 30-year at 5.22% is dollar-positive in the current transmission, as the 1 September session demonstrated when a global bond rout lifted yields, pushed gold to a ten-day low and left the dollar firm; only a confirmed US labour recession is dollar-negative. Against that, the constructive case is genuine and is why confidence is only 48: European equity leadership at record highs reflects real earnings and fiscal-stimulus optimism, and a synchronised expansion is the bottom-of-the-smile configuration in which capital leaves the dollar, which is exactly what the broad index falling 1.69% against the G10 basket's 0.37% has been describing.

The dollar's share of allocated reserves rose to 57.13% in 2026-Q1 from a 56.42% print that was the first sub-57% reading since 1995, the IMF has attributed the majority of past declines to exchange-rate valuation rather than active selling, and the euro's own share fell to 20.03% from 20.38% in the same quarter. So the two structural flows that would carry a strategic long-EUR/USD position both moved against it on the most recent observation, and the bullish case rests on speculative conversion alone - one buyer is not a flow regime.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: On levels this factor favours the base leg decisively and on trajectory it favours the quote leg, which is why the tactical stance is bearish at only modest confidence. The level differential is large: the euro area runs a current-account surplus of 1.7% of GDP against a United States deficit of 2.9%, a 4.6-point gap, and the bilateral relationship is the euro area's largest goods surplus anywhere - EUR exports to the United States of USD 521.1bn against imports of USD 327.8bn for a net USD 193.3bn on IMF Direction of Trade Statistics for 2024. The trajectory runs the other way and it runs through energy. The euro area is the world's largest net energy importer and the United States is now a net energy exporter, so the same shock is a tax on one leg and a subsidy to the other. Dutch TTF front-month gas topped EUR70/MWh on 31 August, the first time since January 2023, with EU storage only 62.99% full on 24 August and the Strait of Hormuz - roughly a fifth of global LNG trade - effectively closed. That is a direct debit to the euro-area goods surplus and a direct credit to US export revenue, and it is the pair's cleanest structural asymmetry. The partial offset is oil: Brent fell 12.0% from USD 100.31 to USD 88.24 over the month, which improves the euro area's import bill and mildly erodes US export receipts, so the two energy legs diverge. Flow data has also been beating on the base leg, with a June euro-area current account of EUR35.1bn against a EUR26.8bn forecast, while the US advance goods balance missed badly at -USD 118.8bn against -USD 100.8bn. Over four weeks the news is mixed; the price signal that determines the next quarter's flows is not.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: At a 0.16 strategic weight this is the second-largest factor and it is a genuine collision between a level that favours the euro and a marginal flow that favours the dollar. The euro-area surplus is eroding fast: EUR276bn or 1.7% of GDP over the twelve months to June 2026, down from EUR305bn and 2.0% a year earlier, with the goods surplus falling from EUR342bn to EUR282bn - a EUR60bn deterioration that is precisely the energy import bill during a period when energy HICP ran at +10.0%. Looking forward the constraint tightens rather than loosens: 62.99% storage against a closed Hormuz means the euro area must buy scarce LNG all autumn in competition with Asia, and Goldman Sachs has said explicitly that current prices will not be enough to manage storage through winter, with December TTF potentially needing to exceed EUR100/MWh. Every EUR10/MWh is a further debit to the base leg and a credit to the quote leg, which sells the same molecule. On the other side, the US position is structurally worse in levels and is deteriorating in composition: a deficit of 2.9% of GDP and widening, a NIIP of minus USD 21.27 trillion, and - the genuinely new fact - a primary income balance that flipped from surplus to deficit in Q1 2026, which attacks the exorbitant-privilege mechanism that has made that NIIP sustainable. Trade policy is also two-sided: the EU-US 15% reciprocal framework took effect on 1 July with autos cut from 27.5% to 15% retroactive to 1 August, capping the tail risk on the euro's USD 193.3bn bilateral surplus, while the retaliation pause expires around early February 2027. Net: the marginal flow over one to six months is the winter energy bill, and it runs against the pair.

net_commodity_exposure.base_commodity_profile: EUR: the world's largest net energy importer. Dutch TTF front-month gas is the critical commodity, above EUR70/MWh on 31 August and the highest since January 2023; the euro area is also a net importer of LNG (JKM-linked) and of crude. Energy contributed +0.94pp of the 2.9% July HICP at +10.0% year on year, and EU storage was 62.99% full on 24 August.
net_commodity_exposure.quote_commodity_profile: USD: a net energy exporter across crude, refined product and LNG. Henry Hub at USD 2.70 is unremarkable while the diesel crack exceeded USD 100/bbl for the first time, so US refining and export economics are strong. The dollar therefore gains on the export channel from precisely the shock that taxes the euro area, in addition to its haven bid.
net_commodity_exposure.net_effect_calculation: Applying the framework's direction rules leg by leg. Natural gas TTF up is a strong negative for the base leg (--EUR) and, because the United States is the marginal LNG exporter into a Hormuz closure that has removed roughly a fifth of global LNG trade, a positive for the quote leg (+USD): net EUR/USD DOWN, and this is the doubly-loaded channel. Oil up is a mild negative for the base leg (-EUR) as an importer and a positive for the quote leg as a net exporter: net EUR/USD DOWN, though weakly. LNG (JKM) up is strongly negative for Asian and European importers and positive for the US exporter: net EUR/USD DOWN. There is no commodity in the pair's exposure set where the base leg is the beneficiary and the quote leg the payer, which is the structural point: unlike a commodity-versus-commodity cross, EUR/USD has no offsetting terms-of-trade leg. Over the current month the two energy prices diverged - Brent fell 12.0% to USD 88.24 while TTF rose above EUR70/MWh - and the divergence is itself the tell, because crude is pricing demand destruction and possible resolution while gas is pricing a physical logistics constraint, and it is the physical constraint that binds for Europe with storage at 62.99%.

The rate channel partially offsets, because higher energy reinforces both central banks' hawkishness and the ECB is the bank with the more incomplete path. Net mildly bearish EUR/USD.

The offset is that it also softens the ECB's inflation case, which is the entire foundation of the euro's rate story, so the flow gain is partly given back through the policy channel. Net mildly bullish EUR/USD, capped.

It is the commodity the euro's own dossier identifies as critical for the base leg, the United States is the marginal seller on the other side of it, and unlike oil it is a physical constraint with a dated seasonal test in November and December against a 62.99% storage level.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: Both central banks are communicating hawkishly, so the bilateral question is not which is more hawkish in tone but which sits further from its own market pricing - and on that test the Fed is the one with room to surprise. The ECB has transmitted its guidance completely: the Account of the 22-23 July meeting, published 27 August, twice described the hold as a pause, stated it was important not to signal the end of the tightening cycle, and judged a further hike likely unless the inflation outlook improved significantly, and within days OIS moved to roughly 97% for 10 September. That is a guidance channel operating at maximum efficiency, which means there is no gap left to arbitrage at the base leg's meeting. The Fed's guidance sits above its own curve: the June SEP median of 3.80% for end-2026 implies a hike outright while futures price 57-66%, the July decision was a 9-3 hold in which all three dissenters wanted to hike - the first three-dissent meeting with a unified direction since September 2016 - and Chair Warsh used the 28 August Jackson Hole keynote to recommit to the 2% PCE objective while citing headline PCE at 3.7% and 4.1% annualised over six months and saying the summer readings do not tell him underlying trends have meaningfully improved. Sequence matters and it favours the quote leg: the ECB moves on 10 September, six days before the FOMC, so the base leg's decision is delivered into a market that already owns it and the quote leg's decision arrives with the surprise capacity intact. The tactical risk to this reading is tonal rather than mechanical - Lagarde acknowledged in July that there is no clear evidence of second-round effects, and repeating that alongside a delivered hike would be a sell-the-fact on the euro, which points the same way.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over one to six months both guidance functions face downward revision risk from their own data, and the two risks are close to symmetric, which is why this is a Neutral rather than a directional input despite a 0.12 weight. On the base leg the market has extrapolated the ECB's hawkishness to a 2.75% terminal by early 2027 that the institution's own arithmetic struggles to support: the negotiated wage tracker printed 2.1% for Q2 2026 against 3.2% in 2025, and the June projections have headline HICP at 2.0% and core at 2.2% in 2028. The 17 December projection round is the specific vehicle, because it is the first vintage in which the 2026 energy base effects come clearly into the 2027 and 2028 window, and a downward revision there reprices the euro strip lower. On the quote leg the Fed's own June SEP already contains the reversal - a 3.80% median for 2026 and 3.60% for 2027 - so the September hike is terminal on the Committee's arithmetic and the 9 December SEP is where that either holds or is removed. Both banks have abandoned explicit forward guidance for meeting-by-meeting data dependence, which raises per-event volatility on both legs symmetrically. The one genuinely asymmetric consideration is institutional rather than analytical and it favours the base leg: the ECB faces no credibility question, while the Fed is operating under public presidential pressure to cut, with analysts framing Jackson Hole as putting the Committee at odds with the Treasury and S&P having explicitly cited credible monetary policy execution in its 26 June AA+ affirmation. That is a low-probability, high-severity dollar-negative tail with no euro-side equivalent, and it offsets the euro's terminal-rate overhang.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: The tactical calendar is dense, clustered and asymmetric against the pair. Four first-order events fall inside a fortnight: US payrolls on 4 September, the ECB with projections on 10 September, US CPI on 11 September and the FOMC with an SEP on 16 September, with the Bank of England and Bank of Japan resolving on 17 and 18 September. Three of those four are quote-leg events, which is the asymmetry that matters - the pair's event risk is concentrated on the American side and only one of them, a second consecutive negative payroll print, is euro-positive. Geopolitically the asymmetry is sharper still and it runs one way. The live theatre is the Gulf, where escalation hits the base leg twice - through the energy import bill and through the euro's explicit lack of haven status - and helps the quote leg twice, through the dollar's haven bid and through US energy export revenue. The most recent news flow is escalatory rather than otherwise: on 31 August Iran's IRGC claimed it downed a US MQ-9 drone over the Strait of Hormuz and attacked a UAE air base, following Iranian strikes on US bases in Jordan, and the July FOMC statement itself cited elevated uncertainty owing in part to the conflict. There is a second one-sided euro-negative in the French 2027 budget process, with a fragmented parliament, record public debt, an OAT-Bund spread of 83.6bp and a Fitch affirmation on 28 August that came with an explicit warning on widening deficits. The quote leg's own event negatives - the 3 November midterms and a 30-year at 5.22% - fall outside the tactical window or, as the 1 September session showed, currently transmit as dollar-supportive.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over one to six months the event balance becomes genuinely two-sided on both legs, and averaging two large ambiguous binaries produces Neutral rather than a direction. The dominant scheduled event is the US midterm congressional election on 3 November, whose FX transmission resists a sign: a result constraining fiscal expansion is dollar-positive through the deficit channel and negative through growth, a result enabling it is the reverse, and how either outcome changes political pressure on a Committee that may have just hiked over presidential objection is unknowable in advance. The Gulf is the second large binary and here the pair's asymmetry cuts the other way from the tactical read: escalation into the northern winter, with 62.99% storage and TTF potentially above EUR100/MWh, is strongly negative for the pair, but a durable ceasefire and Hormuz reopening would collapse both gas and oil, restore the euro area's goods surplus and remove the dollar's haven bid simultaneously - and because the terms-of-trade channel is larger for the base leg than the rate channel it would cost, de-escalation is net positive for the pair by more than escalation is negative per unit of probability. The two branches genuinely offset. The residual one-sided items are small and point in opposite directions: the French 2027 budget is a base-leg negative with a fat left tail located in Paris rather than Rome, and the expiry of the EU's retaliatory-tariff pause around early February 2027 is a dated re-entry point for trade risk on the euro's USD 193.3bn bilateral surplus; against them, a US long-end disorder episode and the tariff legal question - with Section 122 authority lapsed on 24 July and Section 301 duties of 10-12.5% having replaced it the same day, and IEEPA refund mechanics unannounced - are quote-leg negatives of comparable size.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: Neither leg has a dated fiscal event inside the tactical window capable of moving the pair, and the current transmission is inverted in a way that removes any directional read. On the base leg there is no fragmentation stress: the OAT-Bund spread was 83.6bp on 21 August and the 28 August 10-year BTP auction cleared at 4.10% for roughly 81-85bp over the Bund, both far from the levels at which the ECB's Transmission Protection Instrument becomes a live consideration, and auctions are clearing normally across the bloc. Italy has been re-rated after seven upgrades culminating in Moody's Baa2, and France rather than Italy is now the euro area's weaker link, affirmed by Fitch at A+ stable on 28 August with an explicit warning. On the quote leg the arithmetic is materially worse - debt held by the public at 101% of GDP heading to 120% by 2036, a deficit above USD 2 trillion, projected interest costs of USD 1,039 billion which would exceed the post-war high of 3.2% of GDP - and the market is charging for it in the long end, with the 30-year at 5.22%, 2s30s at +88bp, the 20 August 20-year auction stopping at 5.204% against 5.163% previously and the 30-year TIPS clearing at 2.973% against 2.473%, a 50bp jump. But the transmission is the opposite of the intuitive one: on 1 September a global bond rout lifted yields, pushed gold to a ten-day low and left the dollar firm, so a deteriorating quote-leg fiscal position is currently expressed as a dollar-supportive yield rise rather than a dollar-destructive credit event. A structurally euro-favourable differential with no transmission mechanism and no dated catalyst is a Neutral.

strategic.rationale: At strategic weights the framework loads 0.24 on Policy and Rates, 0.16 on External Balance and 0.12 each on Guidance and USD Liquidity, so 64% of the signal sits in four structural factors, and for this pair two of them collide head-on. The bullish structural case is arithmetic rather than narrative. The ECB is priced from 2.25% to 2.50% at the 10 September projection round and to 2.75% by early 2027, while the Fed's own June Summary of Economic Projections has a 3.80% median for end-2026 and 3.60% for 2027 - one more hike and then a cut. If both paths deliver, the bilateral differential narrows from -137.5bp toward -112.5bp by the 9 December FOMC and toward -87.5bp on the Fed's own 2027 dot, and there is no plausible path on which it widens materially. Fiscal reinforces it: projected US interest costs of USD 1,039 billion compound mechanically as low-coupon debt rolls into a 4.5-5.2% curve, a September hike raises that rollover cost directly, and supply now drains bank reserves because the reverse repo facility is empty - while the euro area is absorbing a large German expansion with peripheral spreads contained at 83.6bp and roughly 81-85bp, which is term-premium repricing rather than fragmentation and is the configuration that historically supports the euro. Flows add a residual short euro leg and a dollar long off a three-and-a-half-year high, both with more room to move for the pair than against it. Against that stands a terms-of-trade shock that is equally arithmetic and, crucially, unhedged in this pair. The euro area's twelve-month current-account surplus has fallen from EUR305bn and 2.0% of GDP to EUR276bn and 1.7%, with the goods surplus down EUR60bn from EUR342bn to EUR282bn, and the forward constraint tightens rather than loosens: storage at 62.99% against a closed Strait of Hormuz means Europe buys scarce LNG all autumn in competition with Asia, and Goldman Sachs has said current prices will not be enough to manage the winter with December TTF potentially above EUR100/MWh. Unlike a commodity cross, this pair has no offsetting leg - the United States sells the same molecule. Add an unhedged year-end dollar funding turn with the December 2025 precedent of USD 74.6bn of standing repo usage, and a strategic risk distribution skewed toward higher volatility in which the dollar is the haven and the euro explicitly is not, and the two sides cancel. What is priced versus what we expect produces a specific edge in both directions: the market prices both policy paths roughly correctly, prices no discount at all for a European winter energy squeeze, prices no premium for a US primary income balance that has just flipped to deficit, and prices dollar funding as a solved problem at a basis of minus 0.81bp. The path of least resistance over one to six months is therefore range persistence rather than trend, resolved by which clock runs out first. The dated catalysts are the 28 October FOMC and 29 October ECB back-to-back, the 3 November US midterms, the northern-hemisphere gas test in November and December, the 9 December FOMC SEP and the 17 December ECB projection round eight days later. Conviction is 2 because we can name both sides and size neither, and because the distribution around this central case is wide and left-skewed on the base leg's energy exposure.
strategic.g10_relative_ranking: Strategically the two legs rank level, which is itself the cleanest statement of why this pair is Neutral over one to six months: the standalone dossiers placed the euro 4 of 11 and the dollar 4 of 11, a dead heat, and a pair whose legs rank identically has no cross-sectional edge to harvest. Both lose to the same currencies and for the same reason - external strength that neither can match, with Norway at a 15.6%-of-GDP current-account surplus and direct benefit from the gas shock, Singapore at 16.7% on an appreciating band, and Sweden at 4.5% - so the honest conclusion is that a strategic view on either leg is better expressed against those currencies than against each other. Within its own family, EUR/USD is the euro cross that pays 137.5bp to hold long and offers no terms-of-trade offset, which makes it a worse strategic long than EUR/CHF at +225bp widening to +275bp or EUR/NZD, where the differential changes sign on 10 September, and a worse strategic short than EUR/NOK, where the counter-currency wins on both the rate and the energy channel simultaneously.

cross_horizon_consistency.explanation: The horizons diverge by one notch and the divergence is mechanical rather than a hedge. Three things change. First, Policy and Rates reverses sign at an unchanged 0.24 weight - from -0.1440 to +0.1200, a 0.264 swing that is by itself larger than the entire tactical score - because a 97%-priced ECB hike against a 57-66%-priced FOMC is worthless to the euro over four weeks, while over six months the euro is the leg with the incomplete hiking cycle against a Fed whose own dots contain a 2027 cut, so the differential narrows from -137.5bp toward -87.5bp. Second, the framework re-weights: External Balance rises from 0.06 to 0.16, converting the euro area's energy import bill from a footnote worth -0.0312 into the second-largest force in the table at -0.0832, while Inflation and Growth falls from 0.18 to 0.10 and Guidance rises from 0.07 to 0.12 but turns Neutral as both banks' terminal revision risks become symmetric. Third, two factors genuinely flip on evidence rather than weight: Flows inverts because a spent squeeze on both legs becomes an asymmetric conversion opportunity, and USD Liquidity inverts because the December funding turn falls inside the strategic window and outside the tactical one.
cross_horizon_consistency.inflection_point: The 16 September FOMC with its Summary of Economic Projections, with a secondary confirmation at the 28 October FOMC. That single release resolves the tactical asymmetry - after it, the Fed leg is priced and the pair's rate catalyst is exhausted - and simultaneously sets the strategic path, because the 2027 median dot is what determines whether the September hike is terminal. If the 2027 median holds at or near 3.60% the strategic Neutral is confirmed and the tactical position has an expiry; if it is lifted above 3.60% the September move becomes a cycle and the strategic stance would need upgrading toward the tactical one. The genuine no-man's-land is late September to late October, when neither thesis has an active catalyst.
cross_horizon_consistency.trading_implication: Treat the tactical view as a trade with a defined expiry rather than the opening leg of a strategic position. The asymmetry it rests on - an unpriced Fed leg against a fully priced ECB leg - is consumed on 16 September and does not renew, and beyond that date the differential's direction of travel turns euro-favourable while the euro area's energy bill and the dollar's year-end funding turn take over as the offsetting forces. For anything that must be held across both horizons, the crosses are the answer: the euro's genuine rate advantage is collected with positive carry against the franc or the krona rather than paid for at 137.5bp a year against the dollar, and the dollar's carry advantage is collected more efficiently against the franc, yen or Canadian dollar than against the euro. In level terms, the practical instruction is to be short from 1.1640–1.1700 into 16 September, take profit at 1.1515, and hold nothing outright thereafter unless the December dot plot changes the differential's direction.

A second consecutive contraction after July's −23,000 against a +83,000 consensus would make a hike twelve days later very hard to defend, collapsing the Fed hike pricing that is the pair's dominant bearish input and lifting EUR/USD toward the 1.1700 round number and the 1.17275–1.17759 supply zone; an in-line or better print removes the labour-market objection and lets the 16 September asymmetry play out toward 1.1515. catalysts.event: ECB Governing Council decision with new Eurosystem staff macroeconomic projections
catalysts.rationale: A 25bp move to a 2.50% deposit rate is priced at roughly 97%, so the decision itself cannot pay the base leg twice and the classic pattern for a fully discounted central bank action is spike-and-fade — we expect 40–80 pips of pop that fades within two sessions. The unpriced content is the projection revision against the June baseline of 3.0%, 2.3% and 2.0% headline HICP, and the tone: Lagarde acknowledged in July that there is no clear evidence of second-round effects, and repeating that alongside a delivered hike would be a sell-the-fact on the euro.

catalysts.event: US August CPI (July base 3.4% headline, 2.5% core)
catalysts.rationale: The last inflation print before the FOMC, and the one whose signal is most easily misread for this pair. Core CPI at 2.5% sits 80bp BELOW core PCE at 3.3%, an inversion of the normal sign, and the Fed targets PCE while Warsh quoted headline PCE at 3.7% on 28 August — so a soft core CPI print is less euro-positive than it looks, and a firm one is more dollar-positive than the headline suggests.

catalysts.event: Federal Open Market Committee decision with Summary of Economic Projections
catalysts.rationale: The dominant event in the verdict and the only genuinely two-sided one, priced at 57–66% in futures and 48–55% in prediction markets against a June SEP median of 3.80% that implies the move outright. A delivered hike leaves the differential at −137.5bp and removes the pair's last rate catalyst; a hold strands a same-direction positioning book and squeezes EUR/USD higher through 1.1700. The dot plot released alongside also resets the strategic path, because the 2027 median of 3.60% is what currently makes the hike terminal.

catalysts.event: September quarter-end US dollar funding date
catalysts.rationale: The first quarter-end since reserve balances resumed falling, at USD 2,916bn and heading toward a roughly USD 3 trillion minimum, with the overnight reverse repo facility drained to USD 702 million so there is no absorber left. Tighter dollar funding moves the currency toward the left-hand side of the smile, which is a lower EUR/USD, and a cross-currency basis of −0.81bp shows nobody is hedging it. This is the smaller rehearsal for the year-end turn.

catalysts.event: Federal Open Market Committee decision (no Summary of Economic Projections)
catalysts.rationale: The first Fed meeting after September with no dot plot attached, which makes it the point at which the market must judge on the Committee's silence whether the September move was terminal. This is the identified inflection between the tactical and strategic horizons for the pair: language confirming a plateau leaves the differential set and hands the pair back to the energy and funding channels, while language extending the cycle would reassert the dollar's front-end advantage.

catalysts.event: ECB Governing Council decision (no staff projections)
catalysts.rationale: A non-projection meeting one day after the FOMC, which makes the pair's October repricing effectively a 48-hour bilateral event. The base case is a hold at 2.50%, so the language carries the information: a hold framed as another pause sustains the 2.75% terminal that underpins the strategic bullish rate leg, while a data-dependent framing with softer wage commentary begins the downward repricing that the euro's own 2.1% wage tracker implies.

The dominant scheduled event of the strategic window and genuinely unsignable for the pair. A result constraining fiscal expansion is dollar-positive through the deficit and interest-cost channel that Factor 8 identifies and dollar-negative through growth; a result enabling it is the reverse. The second-order question — how either outcome changes political pressure on a Committee that may have just tightened over presidential objection — is the credibility tail that keeps Guidance Neutral strategically.

catalysts.rationale: The highest-information event of the strategic horizon for this pair and the one with no offsetting leg. Storage at 62.99% against an effectively closed Strait of Hormuz means the base leg must buy scarce LNG in competition with Asia while the quote leg sells it, so every EUR10/MWh on TTF is a direct debit to the euro-area goods surplus and a credit to US export revenue. Goldman Sachs has said current prices will not be enough to manage the winter and that December TTF may need to exceed EUR100/MWh, and the pair carries no visible energy discount at 1.16258.

catalysts.event: Federal Open Market Committee decision with Summary of Economic Projections
catalysts.rationale: The release at which the 2027 median dot of 3.60% — which currently implies a cut back from a September hike and is therefore the foundation of the strategic bullish rate leg for the pair — is either confirmed or removed. Confirmation validates a narrowing differential toward −87.5bp and supports the Neutral; removal converts a terminal hike into a cycle, restores the dollar's front-end advantage and would flip the strategic factor to Bearish.

catalysts.event: ECB Governing Council decision with new Eurosystem staff projections
catalysts.rationale: The pivotal base-leg event of the strategic horizon and the mirror image of the FOMC eight days earlier. This is the first projection vintage in which the 2026 energy base effects come clearly into the 2027 and 2028 window; a downward revision to the 2027 path removes the justification for the 2.75% terminal that the strip carries and reprices the euro strip lower, while evidence of second-round effects finally appearing in the wage and services paths would hold the terminal and confirm the narrowing differential.

The direct analogue of the December 2025 episode, when SOFR-to-IORB spreads reached their widest since 2020 and standing repo usage printed USD 25.95bn on 29 December and a record USD 74.6bn on 31 December before collapsing to zero in January. Every precondition is in place and several are worse, and a cross-currency basis of −0.81bp says the market carries no hedge. Rebranded full-allotment standing repo operations should cap it at pressure rather than crisis, which is exactly the calibration that makes it a EUR/USD negative without being disorderly.

It is also the instrument that distinguishes a rates-driven fall from a funding-driven fall, and the two require different stops and different expressions.

signposts.bilateral_importance: This is the pair's principal strategic dollar-positive and it is entirely absent from consensus forecasts, which treat dollar funding as solved. It is also the one channel that can move EUR/USD without either central bank doing anything.

signposts.current_level: +EUR276bn, or 1.7% of GDP, in the twelve months to June 2026, down from +EUR305bn and 2.0%; goods surplus down from EUR342bn to EUR282bn; the US runs −2.9% and widening, a 4.6-point bilateral gap

signposts.invalidates_if: Stabilises at or above 1.7% in the November and December releases
signposts.bilateral_importance: This is the only signpost that measures the level differential rather than the flow, and it is the reason the strategic stance is Neutral rather than Bearish despite the energy asymmetry: a bloc running a 1.7% surplus with a USD 193.3bn bilateral goods surplus against a −2.9% deficit economy has a structural floor that no other euro cross enjoys.

assumptions: Price payload provenance, quoted verbatim: `dataPoints` 130, `dateRange` 2026-03-06 to 2026-09-03, `spot` 1.16258 and `spotDate` 2026-09-03, with `computationRange` 2008-08-26 to 2026-09-03 (4,695 weekday bars) and `weekendBarsDropped` 0. `dataBasis`: weekday (Mon-Fri) bars from the gated append-only store; SMAs are simple averages of trading-day closes; realised vol annualised on 252. Two `dataQuality` flags: only 2 resistance / 9 support zones met the 2-touch threshold; 4695 weekday bars in the store, 940 weekly, 272 monthly, 130 daily bars passed downstream matching the 1-6 month strategic horizon.

Spot date gap: spotDate is 2026-09-03, two calendar days after the 2026-09-01 valuation date. Every level, target, stop, pip figure, percentage move and distance-to-average in this report is computed against the payload spot of 1.16258 rather than against any fresher web quote, so the document is internally consistent; readers reconciling against a live screen should expect a small offset.

Moving averages and zones: all SMAs are simple arithmetic averages of trading-day closes (SMA50 1.15047, SMA100 1.15662, SMA200 1.16341, SMA200w 1.10668, slope +0.000833/week). The 200-week average is treated as first-class: rising, never closed below in the current sequence, mechanical convergence roughly 67 weeks away. Zones are the payload's computed clusters ranked by touch count; the resistance shortfall (2 zones vs 9 support zones) is supplemented with the 200-day average and round numbers, labelled as supplements.

Volatility, skew and carry: realised volatility is read from the payload (20-day 4.66%, 60-day 4.75%, annualised on 252) rather than recomputed. Implied volatility, risk reversals and butterflies come from the gated CME surface observed 2026-08-31 at 38.6/94.7/185.7-day tenors; the 3-month figure of 5.777% is used verbatim as pair_3m_iv. No one-year IV percentile is asserted as fact; the euro dossier's roughly-8th-percentile estimate is flagged as an estimate.

Forwards are derived, not quoted: the 1/3/6-month outrights are computed from the gated futures roll premium of 139.1bp annualised (observed 2026-08-31, 13.6-to-48.6-day window) applied linearly to payload spot; the basis contribution is negligible (corroborated by CME 3m basis at −0.81bp). No quoted forward-points source was used.

Sovereign yields: both 10-year legs are MONTHLY observations dated 2026-06-01 (EUR 2.97%, USD 4.47%), so the −150bp differential is a like-for-like vintage comparison, not a live spread. Live-level comparisons (Bund 3.29–3.30% on 31 Aug vs UST 4.67% on 27 Aug, ~138bp) are cross-date approximations and labelled as such.

Direction verdict provenance: the ten factor stances, confidences, evidence_type labels, weights, weighted contributions, both net scores, both convictions, both score interpretations, both rationales, both G10 rankings, the cross-horizon consistency block and the catalyst set are carried verbatim from the settled pass-1 verdict, scored without the price payload. Everything price-derived (market context, technicals, volatility, carry, forward decomposition, entries, targets, stops, sizing, scenarios, path expectations, conviction ladders, risk/reward, invalidator levels and signpost thresholds) is this pass's work. Where price argues against the settled tactical direction, that disagreement is stated but not used to re-score factors.

Bilateral trade: goods flows are taken directly from the injected IMF DOTS block for 2024 and not re-estimated (EUR exports to US USD 521.1bn, imports USD 327.8bn, net EUR surplus USD 193.3bn); the figures are two years old at the valuation date, which is normal for DOTS.

Consensus and web research: five searches were run in this pass covering bank forecasts, chart patterns, options skew, dealer positioning, and bilateral investment/hedging flows. No web source was used for spot, performance, moving averages, realised volatility or support/resistance levels. Two mutually exclusive chart-pattern reads (triple-top vs falling wedge) are both reported rather than one being selected. Some search results carried post-valuation timestamps; nothing from those results was used to assert the outcome of post-valuation events.

Percentiles and estimates: the 52-week percentiles of 41 (intraday) and 43 (closing) are computed in the payload. The euro positioning percentile (~30) and dollar percentile (~80) are internal estimates carried from the dossiers, not published series. The BIS REER-relative valuation figures are a real-effective proxy, not a PPP fair value. Scenario probabilities are structured judgements summing to 100% at each horizon, not market-implied.

Weights: default framework weights are applied at both horizons and sum to exactly 1.00. The one arguable adjustment — a Factor 9 boost for proximity to the 200-day average and a five-touch demand zone — was deliberately declined, because raising a weight on the basis of a level seen only in this pass would import chart evidence into a score that was set without it.
